To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CMR is an important non invasive imaging tool to assess myocardial ischemia.
cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an accurate non-invasive method to detect ischemia and to guide decision making in patients with chronic stable coronary artery disease.
cardiac MRI can be used to diagnose ischemia in patients suspected to have coronary artery disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of new CMR techniques to detect myocardial ischemia.
the development of new CMR techniques for the detection of ischemia and its translation into clinical practice.
the development of new methods and applications in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, especially in patients with chronic ischemic heart disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CMR is the gold standard non invasive functional imaging modality for the detection of myocardial ischemic in patients with stable CAD and that CMR should be considered as first line imaging technique in patients with stable coronary artery disease.
CMR is a powerful tool for the detection of myocardial ischemic burden in patients with chronic CAD.
CMR is a highly valuable tool for assessing the presence of ischemia and viability in patients with chronic CAD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cardiac magnetic resonance (CM) has a role in the assessment of ischemia, and in particular, the role of stress perfusion CMR in patients presenting with stable chest pain and/or known coronary artery disease.
CMR is a safe, non-invasive, accurate and reproducible imaging modality for the assessment of myocardium in chronic coronary syndr
cardiac MR imaging is a valuable tool to assess ischemia in patients suffering from chronic coronary syndromies and will play a major role in future diagnostic and therapeutic decision making.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CMR is a valuable imaging modality for detecting myocardial ischemia.

CMR is an important imaging technique for the diagnosis of myocardial ischemic disease in the setting of chronic coronary syndomes and that it should be considered as a first line diagnostic tool in the future.

CMR can be used as a gatekeeper to coronary angiography and that CMR based strategies are at least as effective in terms of hard clinical outcomes as invasive strategies in patients with chronic stable coronary syndromes.
